body.p: Intel® Total Storage Encryption (TSE) provides a security measure for a PCIe NVMe device by encrypting the data in the device using the Intel inline encryption.

The Intel® Total Storage Encryption, is enabled through BIOS configuration. TSE encrypts the data using the AES XTS algorithm with a 256-bit data encryption key and 256-bit tweak key when the data is written to the NVMe storage from system memory and decrypted when read from the storage to the system memory.

The OS software can wrap the 256-bit keys using Platform Bind Key BLOB (PBNDKB) instruction and get the key handle wrapped by a platform-specific wrapping key. Once the software obtains the handle, the software can delete the original keys from memory. The software can also program the 256-bit keys using either the key handles or plaintext keys through the Platform Config (PCONFIG) instruction. Please refer to the Intel® Architecture Instruction Set Extensions Programming Reference document for PBNDKB ISA.

The CPU PCONFIG/PBNDKB ISA is used by the OS to generate keys for the crypto operations and creates the Intel® Total Storage Encryption table in the system memory so that the TSE HW can look up the table to identify the Key ID with tweak value based on the physical address accessed through the storage driver of the PCIe-NVMe device. BitLocker could use the TSE as security enhancement through BitLocker Drive Encryption configuration besides OS managed software encryption using AES-NI instruction sets.
